channel.title: The daily tape · compute.world
channel.description: Anthropic's second IPO filing amendment, filed Tuesday, says its August 2026 compute agreement with Lambda, about $34.9 billion of a $41.3 billion set of Lambda commitments, is now terminable by either party because Lambda did not secure the facility lease by the contractual date; neither side has given notice and Anthropic says it does not intend to terminate. The same filing lifts its Microsoft commitment to at least $47.2 billion. Hours later CoreWeave reported Q3 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168%, raised 2026 guidance and showed backlog of $132.5 billion, up from $104.2 billion in June, while saying it will avoid parent-level unsecured debt through 2027 at current yields. CEO Michael Intrator argued that if sector construction slows, installed compute gets scarcer and GPU pricing may stay higher for longer. TSMC's October revenue hit NT$586.9 billion, up 59.7% year on year and its highest month on record. BloombergNEF counts 181 GW of on-site gas proposed for data centres in the US and Europe as builders route around grid queues. Live list prices held for a third straight day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks and 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.

Countries: United States: Anthropic S-1/A: $34.9 billion August Lambda agreement terminable after a missed facility-lease deadline; no notice given (Wire, 10 Nov, confirmed). United States: CoreWeave Q3 revenue $3.66 billion, backlog $132.5 billion, 1.85 GW active by end-2026 reaffirmed (Wire, 10 Nov, confirmed). Malaysia: Google commits US$15 billion for 2027 to 2028 campuses in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan plus more than 1 GW of clean energy (Wire, 4 Nov, confirmed). United States: Kraft Group floats a 900 MW, $16 billion campus in Sutton, Massachusetts; town vote targeted May 2027 (Wire, 11 Nov, single-source). United States: Integra-linked TDLR filing for an $8 billion, up to 756 MW campus in Quanah, Texas (Wire, 10 Nov, single-source).
